title: Stanley–Stembridge Conjecture
statement_text: Unit interval graphs have chromatic symmetric functions that expand positively in the $e$-basis of the ring $\mathrm{Sym}$ of symmetric functions.
context_text: Proposed by Stanley and Stembridge in 1993 and reformulated by Guay-Paquet in 2013, this conjecture has driven a large body of research on the chromatic symmetric function $X_G$. The paper shows that the conjecture does not have a K-theoretic lift: the Kromatic symmetric functions $\overline{X}_{P_n}$ of path graphs are not positive in either of two proposed K-analogues of the $e$-basis.
paper_contribution: Demonstrates that the Stanley–Stembridge conjecture does not lift to K-theory, as $\overline{X}_{P_3}$ is not positive in either of two natural K-theoretic deformations of the $e$-basis, suggesting the conjecture is unlikely to be amenable to a topological/Schubert-calculus approach.
paper_title: The Kromatic Symmetric Function: A $K$-theoretic Analogue of $X_G$

title: Grassmannian Subvariety Construction Problem
statement_text: For each claw-free incomparability graph $G$, there should exist a subvariety of the Grassmannian whose cohomology class is represented by $X_G$ and whose K-theoretic structure sheaf class is represented by $\overline{X}_G$. It would be very interesting to have an explicit construction of such subvarieties.
context_text: For a graph $G$, Stanley's chromatic symmetric function is $X_G=\sum_\kappa\prod_{v\in V(G)}x_{\kappa(v)}$, the sum over all proper colourings $\kappa:V(G)\to\mathbb{N}$. The Kromatic symmetric function $\overline{X}_G=\sum_\kappa\prod_{v\in V(G)}\prod_{i\in\kappa(v)}x_i$ is its $K$-theoretic analogue, where now $\kappa$ ranges over all proper set colourings, assigning to each vertex a non-empty finite set of colours so that adjacent vertices receive disjoint sets. The incomparability graph of a poset $P$ has vertex set $P$, two elements being adjacent when they are incomparable; it is claw-free (no induced $K_{1,3}$) exactly when $P$ is $(3+1)$-free. In the ring of symmetric functions, viewed as the cohomology of Grassmannians, Schur functions $s_\lambda$ represent Schubert classes; in $K$-theory they are replaced by symmetric Grothendieck functions $\overline{s}_\lambda$, representing structure sheaves of Schubert varieties. Gasharov proved that $X_G$ is Schur-positive for every claw-free incomparability graph $G$; the authors' main result lifts this to $K$-theory: $\overline{X}_G$ is a positive sum of symmetric Grothendieck functions. Since all known proofs of Gasharov's theorem are representation-theoretic or combinatorial, the authors suggest that both results should have a topological interpretation, and propose finding explicit subvarieties realising them. In contrast they show that Kromatic symmetric functions of paths are not positive in several $K$-analogues of the $e$-basis, so the Stanley–Stembridge conjecture does not lift in this way. This is a speculative remark in algebraic combinatorics rather than a precise conjecture.

paper_title: The Kromatic Symmetric Function: A $K$-theoretic Analogue of $X_G$
